headline: A last day of autumn shooting at Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt spends the whole day hunting the woods and fields around Oyster Bay, bagging squirrels, rabbits and quail despite poor aim. He caps a fine week of crisp fall weather with evenings of reading and whist with his mother and sisters, and his brother Elliott arrives that night.

events.detail: Tramps the woods all day and bags two squirrels, three rabbits and five quail
Evening by the fire reading and playing whist with his mother and sisters
Brother Elliott joins the family in the evening

tr_quotes.text: Went out shooting, spending the whole day tramping about through the woods and fields. Game was plenty but I shot badly
2 squirrel 3 rabbit 5 quail.

uncertain: The 'two sweet girls' are presumably his sisters Bamie and Conie, but the diary does not name them.

headline: Leaving Oyster Bay for New York
summary: Reluctantly leaving Oyster Bay, Roosevelt heads into New York and stays the night at his Uncle Jim's. That evening he calls on the visiting Lee family, whom his mother and sisters are entertaining with a round of outings all week.

events.detail: Goes from Oyster Bay to New York, lodging at his uncle's
Calls on the Lees, in town on a visit

tr_quotes.text: In the afternoon I left Oyster Bay with much reluctance and came in to New York to spend the night at Uncle Jim's.

uncertain: 'Uncle Jim' is taken to be James King Gracie; the diary gives only the nickname.

headline: On to Boston
summary: Roosevelt leaves New York and returns to Boston, heading back to college.

events.detail: Travels from New York back to Boston

tr_quotes.text: Went on to Boston.

headline: Back to the books at Harvard
summary: Back in Cambridge, Roosevelt throws himself into his studies, determined to catch up on everything he missed within the week.

events.detail: Resumes his coursework, aiming to recover lost ground by week's end

tr_quotes.text: Started studying with a will; by the end of this week I shall make up all I have lost.

headline: Driving out with Harry Shaw
summary: Roosevelt takes his friend Harry Shaw on a drive to the Lyman home, then has dinner with the Saltonstall family.

events.detail: Drives Harry Shaw to visit the Lymans
Dines with the Saltonstalls

tr_quotes.text: Drove Harry Shaw over to the Lymans, afterwards dined at the Saltonstalls.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard in Cambridge; nothing else is recorded for the day.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is in Cambridge at college, with no other details for the day.

headline: Dinner at the Whitneys, night at the Minots
summary: Roosevelt makes a round of calls by carriage, from the Saltonstalls to the Whitneys, where he enjoys dinner and finds himself growing fonder of Bessie Whitney. He ends at Harry Minot's house for the night, with whist and billiards among the young men of several families.

events.detail: Morning drive to the Saltonstalls, then dinner with the Whitneys
Spends the night at Harry Minot's, with whist and billiards among friends

tr_quotes.text: Miss Bessie I like more and more

headline: Sunday school, and a talk on machine politics
summary: Roosevelt hurries back to Cambridge to teach his Sunday school class and spends the evening with Lulu Lane. At an O.K. Society meeting he speaks about political machines, drawing on New York's recent election, and classmate Frederick Almy notes in his own diary that the talk sparked a lively discussion.

events.detail: Returns in time to teach his Sunday school class
Spends the evening with Lulu Lane
Speaks to the O.K. Society on machine politics, citing New York's latest election

tr_quotes.text: Drove back to Cambridge in time for my Sunday School. Passed the evening very pleasantly with pretty Lulu Lane.

references.title: Theodore Roosevelt, The Formative Years (Carleton Putnam), quoting Frederick Almy's diary

headline: Evening at the Lees
summary: Roosevelt drives out to the Lee family's home, stays for dinner and a long evening, and doesn't get back until after eleven. He is pleased with how well his new horse and cart are running.

events.detail: Dines with the Lees and stays late into the night

tr_quotes.text: The horse and cart go beautifully.

headline: A rueful note to Bamie
summary: Roosevelt writes to his sister Bamie, grumbling about how fickle women can be, as he senses that Alice Lee is turning him away.

events.detail: Writes Bamie a wry complaint about female fickleness

letters.topic: Complains about women's changing moods amid his troubled courtship

tr_quotes.text: Oh, the changeableness of the female mind.

headline: Club life and late nights at Harvard
summary: After taking Minot Weld on a drive to the Saltonstalls and a walk with Rose Lee and Rose Saltonstall, Roosevelt reflects in his diary on his college routine: free hours at his club and the A.D., many outings, hard study and late nights, all carried on the strength of his summer conditioning.

events.detail: Drives Minot Weld to the Saltonstalls and walks out with Rosy and Rose
Reflects in his diary on club life, study and his physical stamina

tr_quotes.text: I spend most of my spare time in Cambridge in the club; and I also go a good deal to the A.D., where the fellows are very pleasant and intellectual - a rare thing with college boys.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is at college in Cambridge; the day has no other entry.

headline: To New York for the Princeton game
summary: Roosevelt travels to New York to watch Harvard's football team take on Princeton. Classmates Jack Tebbets and Harry Chapin come along as his guests, planning to return to Boston on Monday with Bamie and Conie, who are bound for a week at Chestnut Hill.

events.detail: Goes to New York to see Harvard play Princeton at football

tr_quotes.text: Went on to New York to see our football team play Princeton

headline: Harvard loses; a night on the town
summary: Harvard's football team goes down to defeat. Roosevelt calls on Grace Potter, has Fanny Smith to dinner, then takes in the theater, supper at Delmonico's and a long, song-filled night at the Harvard Club.

events.detail: Watches Harvard lose its football game to Princeton
Visits Grace Potter; Fanny Smith dines with the family
Theater, then supper at Delmonico's and a late night at the Harvard Club

tr_quotes.text: Our team was beaten.

uncertain: Header lists Princeton, but the diary suggests Roosevelt spent the day in New York; the game's location is not stated.

headline: A Sunday visit with Edith Carow
summary: Roosevelt enjoys a familiar family Sunday in New York; the family takes warmly to his friend Jack Tebbets. He lunches with Aunt Annie and pays a delightful call on his childhood friend Edith Carow, whom he calls the best-read girl he knows.

events.detail: Spends Sunday with the family and lunches with Aunt Annie
Calls on Edith Carow

tr_quotes.text: she is the most cultivated, best read girl I know.

headline: Back to Boston with his sisters
summary: Roosevelt returns to Boston with Bamie and Conie and attends a class meeting that night. His sisters settle in at Chestnut Hill, where the Saltonstalls host a dinner in their honor.

events.detail: Returns to Boston accompanied by his sisters
Attends a class meeting in the evening
Bamie and Conie are honored at a Saltonstall dinner

tr_quotes.text: Came on to Boston with the girls. Class meeting at night.

headline: A runaway ride home from the Lees
summary: On a rainy day Roosevelt and Dick Saltonstall drive a buggy to dinner with the Lees, followed by an evening of dancing and talk with friends. On the way home a brandy-fueled Dick gallops the horse, which bolts several times, leaving Roosevelt helpless with laughter.

events.detail: Dinner and dancing at the Lees with Dick Saltonstall and friends
Dick whips the horse into repeated runaways on the drive home

tr_quotes.text: I nearly died laughing.

headline: Another evening at the Lees
summary: Roosevelt brings Jack Tebbets to dinner at the Lees, and the evening passes in dancing and games.

events.detail: Dinner, dancing and games at the Lees with Jack Tebbets

headline: Through the snow to the Saltonstalls
summary: In a heavy snowfall, Roosevelt and Dick Saltonstall drive over to the Saltonstall home for dinner.

events.detail: Drives with Dick through the snow to dine with the Saltonstalls

tr_quotes.text: Snowing heavily; Dick + I drove over to the Saltonstalls for dinner.

headline: Dinner with the Lawrences
summary: Roosevelt has dinner with the Lawrence family and enjoys a pleasant evening.

events.detail: Dines with the Lawrences

tr_quotes.text: Dined at the Lawrences passing a very pleasant evening.

headline: A 34-guest luncheon at the Porcellian
summary: Roosevelt hosts a grand lunch for 34 at the Porcellian Club in honor of Bamie and Corinne, with the Lees, Saltonstalls, Whitneys and many classmates at the table. Flowers, food, wine and witty toasts all land well. He finishes the day at a small party at the Minots.

events.detail: Hosts a luncheon for 34 at the Porcellian Club honoring his sisters
Evening drive to a small party at the Minots

tr_quotes.text: It was the greatest success imaginable.
Everything went off to perfection; the dinner was capital, the flowers very pretty and we had great fun with the toasts and speeches.

uncertain: The guest list is long and partly hard to read in the record; only clearly legible names are listed. 'Mr. Saltonstall' is assumed to be Leverett Saltonstall.

headline: Sisters' last day in Boston
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts at his club, makes a trip out to Chestnut Hill, and returns to teach Sunday school. His sisters, who have loved their stay, head home the next day.

events.detail: Breakfast at the club and a drive to Chestnut Hill
Teaches his Sunday school class

tr_quotes.text: It has been very pleasant to have them on here, and they have enjoyed themselves greatly.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard; no other details survive for the day.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is in Cambridge at college; the record is blank otherwise.

headline: Settling in with the Saltonstalls
summary: Roosevelt lunches with the Lees, drives Rose Lee to the Lawrences' for tennis and takes her on a long drive afterward. He then moves in with the Saltonstalls through Sunday, feeling completely at home with the whole family, and plays whist in the evening.

events.detail: Lunch at the Lees, then drives Rosy to a Lawrence tennis party
Begins a stay with the Saltonstall family until Sunday

tr_quotes.text: I am now most thoroughly and happily at home here, and I really love every member of the family.

headline: Thanksgiving dinner with the Lees
summary: Roosevelt takes Rose Saltonstall out in the dog cart and goes skating with young Phil before heading to the Lees at four for Thanksgiving dinner. The evening dissolves into games, dancing and charades.

events.detail: Drives Rose Saltonstall out in the dog cart
Goes skating with Phil
Thanksgiving dinner and charades at the Lees

tr_quotes.text: Afterwards we had great fun, playing games, dancing + acting charades.

uncertain: Phil is presumably a Saltonstall child; the surname is not given.

headline: Rain, candy and late-night theology
summary: Caught in the rain on a long cart ride with Alice Lee, Roosevelt must beg an umbrella at a stranger's door. Later he walks with Alice and Rose, who tease him into buying candy, and stays up talking poetry and theology with Mr. Saltonstall long after Mrs. Saltonstall dozes off.

events.detail: Long cart ride with Alice; rain forces him to borrow an umbrella
Afternoon walk with Alice and Rose
Talks poetry and theology late into the night with Mr. Saltonstall

tr_quotes.text: I stayed up till all hours with dear old Mr. Saltonstall, talking poetry and theology

uncertain: 'Mr. Saltonstall' assumed to be Leverett Saltonstall.

headline: A rainy day of stories and dancing
summary: Kept indoors by rain, Roosevelt reads, dances with Mamie and Hattie and tells stories to the younger children. After lunch he walks out with Ell Whitney, Rose and Alice, calls on Julia Bacon, and spends the evening at the Lees.

events.detail: Spends a rainy morning reading, dancing and telling the children stories
Walks with Ell Whitney, Rose and Alice, then visits Julia Bacon
Evening of dancing and whist at the Lees

tr_quotes.text: telling stories to Phil + Cotty

headline: Five lovely days end
summary: After church, Roosevelt sadly leaves Chestnut Hill and drives back to Cambridge, teaching Sunday school and spending the evening at the Whitneys. Privately he has lost hope of winning Alice Lee, and friends find him roaming the wintry Cambridge woods without purpose.

events.detail: Attends church, then teaches Sunday school
Drives from Chestnut Hill back to Cambridge
Takes tea with the Whitneys

tr_quotes.text: After Church I left the Hill, with the deepest regret that the lovely five days were over

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard; nothing more is noted for the day.

headline: Alice and Rose make their debut
summary: Roosevelt attends a party at the Wares that marks the society debut of Alice Lee and Rose Saltonstall, and enjoys watching the crowd of debutantes. He resolves to go out into society this winter.

events.detail: Attends the coming-out party for Alice and Rose at the Wares

tr_quotes.text: I am going out into society this winter.

headline: Supper at the Porc
summary: Roosevelt has a small supper at the Porcellian Club.

events.detail: Small supper at the Porcellian

tr_quotes.text: Had a little supper up in the Porc.

headline: Overnight at Minot Weld's
summary: Roosevelt drives Jack Tebbets and Minot Weld to the Weld home, where they stay the night, and goes on to an enjoyable party at the Grays after dinner.

events.detail: Drives with Jack Tebbets to stay overnight at Minot Weld's
Attends a party at the Grays

headline: Dinner at the Lees, a drive to Boston
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge in the morning, drives out to the Lees for dinner, and then takes Frank Lee into Boston.

events.detail: Returns to Cambridge
Dines with the Lees
Drives Frank Lee into Boston

headline: Seven-fifteen every morning

events.detail: Day at Minot Weld's, dinner at Harry Shaw's in Boston
Evening card party with Miss Silsbee

tr_quotes.text: I enjoy my horse and cart more and more every day.

headline: Sunday school is thriving
summary: Roosevelt reports that his Sunday school class is doing well, then takes tea with the Lane sisters and enjoys the evening.

events.detail: Teaches his Sunday school class
Takes tea with the Misses Lane

tr_quotes.text: My Sunday School is getting along swimmingly.

headline: Nightly whist and a spree
summary: Roosevelt plays his regular evening whist at the club with Jack, Dick and Minot, a nightly habit, and then the four go out on a lively spree.

events.detail: Whist at the club with his regular foursome, then a night out

headline: A grand party at the Amorys
summary: Roosevelt dines with Emmons Blaine at Harry Shaw's and then goes on to a large party given by the Amory family.

events.detail: Dinner with Emmons Blaine at Harry Shaw's
Attends a big party at the Amorys

headline: Dinner with the Lanes
summary: Roosevelt dines with the Lane family, who have been kind to him; he is especially fond of Lulu Lane.

events.detail: Dines at the Lanes'

tr_quotes.text: They have been very sweet to me, and I like them both very much, especially pretty miss Lulu.

headline: Dancing at the first Harvard Assembly
summary: At the season's first Harvard Assembly Roosevelt dances happily with Rose Lee. Back in Cambridge afterward, he and friends hold a small 'Symposium'.

events.detail: Dances with Rosy Lee at the opening Harvard Assembly
Late-night gathering with friends back at Harvard

tr_quotes.text: dancing with Rosy Lee, who looked as pretty as a picture.

headline: A quiet day in Cambridge
summary: Roosevelt is in Cambridge; no other entry exists for the day.

headline: A three-mile run and a night at the theater
summary: Roosevelt runs three miles in the morning, at an easy 21 minutes. He drives Jack and Dick to Chestnut Hill after lunch, then heads into town with Harry Chapin for dinner at Young's and a play.

Drives Jack and Dick out to Chestnut Hill
Dinner at Young's and the theater with Harry Chapin

events.detail: Teaches Sunday school
Tea at the Minots with Harry Chapin and Howard Townsend

headline: Lulu Lane is engaged

Dances with Nana Rotch at the season's first Papanti party

headline: A comic play at the Gaiety
summary: After dinner at the Amorys, Roosevelt goes with Harry Chapin and Jack Tebbets to see a comedy at the Gaiety that has them laughing.

events.detail: Dines at the Amorys, then sees a comedy with friends

headline: Hasty Pudding theatricals

events.detail: Drives Tom Lee to the Saltonstalls
Attends the Hasty Pudding theatricals

tr_quotes.text: Pudding Theatricals in the evening, very good.

headline: Champagne supper and D.K.E. theatricals
summary: Roosevelt takes Dick for a drive and calls on the Lanes and Rotches. That night brings a champagne dinner, a D.K.E. stage show he ranks above any he has seen, and a nightcap of punch at the club.

events.detail: Drives Dick out and calls on the Lanes and Rotches
Champagne dinner, D.K.E. theatricals and punch at the club

headline: Night boat to New York
summary: Roosevelt and Harry Chapin board the overnight boat bound for New York at the start of the holidays.

events.detail: Takes the night boat to New York with Harry Chapin

headline: Home for the holidays
summary: Roosevelt arrives in New York and is overjoyed to be reunited with his family.

events.detail: Reaches New York and rejoins his family

tr_quotes.text: It is perfectly delightful to see all the family again.

headline: Sunday with the Roosevelt cousins
summary: After church Roosevelt spends the day with his Roosevelt relatives, and his cousin West, known as Doc, stays the night.

events.detail: Attends church
Day with his Roosevelt cousins; West stays over

headline: Ike Iselin's dinner

events.detail: Guest of honor at a dinner hosted by Ike Iselin

tr_quotes.text: We had capital fun.

headline: Sleighing to Jerome Park

events.detail: Sleigh drive with Elliott to dinner at Jerome Park
Harvard Glee Club supper at the University Club

headline: Christmas Eve calls
summary: Roosevelt spends Christmas Eve making the rounds of New York friends, including Annie Murray, Emily Post, Edith Carow, Fanny Smith and the Kane and Potter sisters.

events.detail: Visits a long list of friends around the city

headline: Christmas and the newsboys' dinner

Supervises the Christmas dinner for newsboys with Elliott
Annual Roosevelt family Christmas dinner

headline: Chestnut Hill friends arrive
summary: Roosevelt has lunch with Edith Carow. That evening Alice Lee, Rose Lee, Rose Saltonstall, Dick Saltonstall, Harry Shaw and Ell Whitney arrive from Boston to stay with the family for a week.

events.detail: Lunches with Edith Carow
Boston friends arrive for a week-long stay

Small party at Aunt Annie's

events.detail: Spends the afternoon at the Newsboys' Lodging House

tr_quotes.text: Spent the afternoon at the Newsboys Lodging house.

Theater party hosted by Aunt Lizzie

Theater and supper with Elliott and the whist club

headline: Off to old Salem
summary: Roosevelt travels to Salem with Alice, Rose, Mrs. Lee and Mrs. Saltonstall, lodging in a curious old house owned by Miss Saltonstall, and enjoys a lively party at Hamilton Hall.

events.detail: Goes to Salem with the Saltonstall and Lee ladies
Party at Hamilton Hall

headline: Back from Salem
summary: Roosevelt returns from Salem, dines at Theodore Lyman's and finishes with a small spree at the Porcellian.

events.detail: Returns from Salem
Dinner at Theodore Lyman's
Late gathering at the Porcellian

headline: Alice Lee says yes
summary: Nearly eight months after his first proposal, Roosevelt drives to the Lees determined to settle things, and after long pleading Alice Lee agrees to marry him. In a rapturous diary entry he vows to devote his life to her happiness and gives thanks to God.

events.detail: Alice Lee accepts his proposal of marriage
Pours out his joy and his vows to Alice in his diary

tr_quotes.text: At last everything is settled; but it seems impossible to realize it. I am so happy that I dare not trust in my own happiness.
after much pleading my own sweet, pretty darling consented to be my wife.

uncertain: Engagement kept private for now; the diary notes a word crossed out in the original.

headline: Semiannual exams begin
summary: Roosevelt sits the first of his midyear examinations, then dances at the Papanti Hall party, where Alice is the belle of the room and gives him her favor.

events.detail: Takes the first of the semiannual exams
Papanti Hall party; Alice gives him her favor

tr_quotes.text: she gave me her favour.

headline: Afraid it won't last
summary: Only now beginning to grasp his engagement, Roosevelt confesses a lingering fear that Alice may change her mind, as she has before.

events.detail: Records his doubts about the engagement in his diary

tr_quotes.text: I am only just beginning to realize it

headline: Hinting at big news
summary: Roosevelt looks in on a little gathering at the Parkman Shaws', though parties have lost their appeal this winter. He writes Bamie that he has important news to share, promising to reveal it when he comes home at week's end.

events.detail: Small gathering at the Parkman Shaw home
Teases Bamie with news he will deliver in person

letters.topic: Promises to share important news on his coming trip home

tr_quotes.text: I have a pretty important piece of information to impart.

headline: A day with his sweetheart
summary: Roosevelt lunches with the Saltonstalls, spends the afternoon with Alice, dines with Frank Lee at the Union Club and closes the evening at the Horticultural Assembly, where Alice looks lovelier than ever.

events.detail: Lunch at the Saltonstalls and an afternoon with Alice
Dinner with Frank Lee at the Union Club
Attends the Horticultural Assembly with Alice

headline: Looking back on months of torment
summary: Roosevelt reflects on the four months of anguish behind him, sleepless nights over Alice that no one else suspected. He admits it was love at first sight and his first love.

events.detail: Reflects in his diary on his long, secret courtship

tr_quotes.text: I have been pretty nearly crazy, over my wayward, wilful darling.
It was a real case of love at first sight - and my first love to.

headline: Telling the family
summary: Roosevelt travels to New York to break the news of his engagement; the family is thrilled and very surprised. His mother writes to Alice Lee.

events.detail: Goes home to New York
Announces his engagement to the family
Mittie writes to Alice Lee

tr_quotes.text: who of course were all perfectly delighted and too sweet for anything, though very much surprised.

uncertain: The letter from Mittie to Alice is not one TR wrote or received, so it is not listed under letters.

headline: Sharing the news with uncles and aunts
summary: Roosevelt tells his uncles and aunts about the engagement and they are delighted. He still feels he must be dreaming.

events.detail: Informs the wider family of his engagement

tr_quotes.text: I still feel as if I were in a dream; it is too good to be true.

headline: Choosing a diamond ring
summary: Roosevelt selects a diamond engagement ring for Alice and returns to Boston that afternoon.

events.detail: Picks out a diamond ring for Alice
Returns to Boston

tr_quotes.text: Chose a diamond ring for my darling

headline: Upset in a snowdrift
summary: In heavy snow Roosevelt sleighs to Chestnut Hill, his horse sinking to its belly in drifts, to see Alice. On the way home the sleigh overturns and he is dragged some 300 yards clinging to the reins. Alice writes his mother that she loves him deeply.

events.detail: Sleighs through deep drifts to Chestnut Hill
Visits Alice
Thrown in a drift and dragged about 300 yards before stopping the horse
Evening party at the Rotches

tr_quotes.text: Coming home I was upset in a great drift, and dragged about 300 yards, holding on to the reins, before I could stop the horse.

uncertain: The record also notes Alice's letter to Mittie, which is not TR's own correspondence.

headline: Keeping the secret
summary: Roosevelt and Dick go for a long sleigh ride in perfect sleighing weather. The engagement won't be made public until a week from Monday, and staying away from Alice is hard.

events.detail: Long sleigh drive with Dick

tr_quotes.text: it is awfully hard to- keep away from her.

headline: Harvard Assembly with Lulu Lowell
summary: Roosevelt dances with Lulu Lowell at the Harvard Assembly.

events.detail: Dances with Lulu Lowell at the Harvard Assembly

headline: Almost too happy
summary: Roosevelt sleighs over to the Saltonstalls, dines there and spends the evening with Alice.

events.detail: Dinner at the Saltonstalls and an evening with Alice

tr_quotes.text: I am almost too happy.

headline: A great Porcellian supper
summary: Roosevelt drives Minot Weld home and back, and attends a big supper at the Porcellian in the evening.

events.detail: Round-trip drive with Minot Weld
Porcellian Club supper

headline: A new mission school and a tribute to friends
summary: Roosevelt begins teaching at a mission school in East Cambridge. In his diary he praises his circle of friends, led by Elliott, as plucky, honorable and sensible, and declares his happiness complete now that Alice is his. He ends the day with tea at the Whitneys.

events.detail: Starts teaching at a mission school in East Cambridge
Lists his closest friends in his diary
Tea and evening at the Whitneys
Writes his mother that he saw Alice only twice last week

letters.topic: Mentions seeing Alice only twice during the past week

tr_quotes.text: I have certainly got a marvellously hightoned and honorable set of friends; they are not brilliant, but they are plucky, honourable and rigidly virtuous, and with plenty of common sense.
I only saw Alice twice last week.

uncertain: 'Jack Elliott' is listed as written; his identity is unclear.

headline: A below-zero sleigh ride
summary: Roosevelt dines at Jim Parker's and dances with Nana Rotch at the Papanti party. Afterward he and Dick ride out to Chestnut Hill in Dick's cutter with the thermometer below zero, so bundled up they hardly notice.

events.detail: Dinner at Jim Parker's, then the Papanti party with Nana Rotch
Night sleigh ride to Chestnut Hill in subzero cold

tr_quotes.text: it was a splended sleigh ride.

headline: Nothing to hide from Alice
summary: Roosevelt drives back to Cambridge and goes to a party at the Winthrops. In his diary he gives thanks that he has nothing in his past he could not tell Alice.

events.detail: Returns to Cambridge
Evening party at the Winthrops
Reflects on his clean conscience toward Alice

tr_quotes.text: Thank heaven I am absolutely pure. I can tell Alice everything I have ever done.

headline: Sleighing to the Lowells for leap year
summary: Seven friends pile into a sleigh bound for the Lowells' leap year gathering, where Alice is among the guests.

events.detail: Sleighs with six friends to a leap year party

headline: Presiding at an A.D. dinner
summary: Roosevelt presides over an A.D. Club dinner for 25 in Boston and counts it among the best he has attended, full of good songs, stories and speeches.

events.detail: Presides over an A.D. Club dinner for 25 men

tr_quotes.text: It was one of the pleasantest dinners I have ever been to

headline: Storm-bound with his 'Little Sunshine'
summary: Roosevelt drives through hard rain to dine with the Lees and, thanks to the storm, stays the night. He fills his diary with devotion to Alice, his 'Little Sunshine', and writes Henry Minot to announce the engagement.

events.detail: Dines with the Lees and is kept overnight by the storm
Writes at length in his diary about his love for Alice
Tells Henry Minot of his engagement

letters.topic: Shares the news of his engagement to Alice Lee

tr_quotes.text: I do not think ever a man loved a woman more than I love her

headline: Champagne for the club
summary: On Valentine's Day Roosevelt returns to Cambridge, tells his club about the engagement and buys champagne for all. He spends the evening at the Fish family's leap year dance.

events.detail: Drives back to Cambridge
Announces his engagement to the Porcellian and treats members to champagne
Leap year dance at the Fish home

tr_quotes.text: announced my engagement to the Club, and 'set up' champagne.

headline: A snowy drive with Alice
summary: After Sunday school Roosevelt drives to the Lees and takes Alice for a long ride as snow begins to fall, then spends the evening and night there.

events.detail: Teaches Sunday school
Long drive with Alice in the snow; stays overnight

tr_quotes.text: how pretty the little witch looked!

headline: A boxing benefit
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge early and goes into Boston in the evening for a boxing benefit.

events.detail: Returns to Cambridge
Attends a boxing benefit in Boston

headline: The family comes to meet Alice
summary: Roosevelt goes into Boston to greet his family, who have come to see Alice, and brings Elliott back to stay the night with him.

events.detail: Meets his family on their arrival in Boston
Elliott spends the night with him

headline: Forty-two bouquets
summary: Roosevelt drives Elliott to lunch at the Saltonstalls, where his whole family gathers. He spends the afternoon with Alice, dines at the Lees and stays late at the Porcellian. Alice has received 42 bouquets.

events.detail: Lunch at the Saltonstalls with Elliott and the family
Afternoon with Alice, dinner with the Lees
Hours at the Porcellian

tr_quotes.text: Alice has received 42 bouquets.

headline: Theater party for Bamie and Conie
summary: Roosevelt drives Elliott into Boston, dines with his family at the Brunswick and joins a theater party that Frank and Tom Lee give for his sisters, with Alice acting as chaperone. He also accepts Henry Minot's invitation to dinner for himself and Alice on March 1.

events.detail: Family dinner at the Brunswick Hotel
Theater party for his sisters hosted by Frank and Tom Lee
Accepts a March 1 dinner invitation from Henry Minot

letters.topic: Accepts a dinner invitation for himself and Alice on March 1

tr_quotes.text: I sat by pretty Miss Sunshine, who 'matronized'!

headline: Up all night after the Pudding
summary: After a family day and a big family dinner at the Lees, Roosevelt drives home by moonlight and joins a rowdy night at the Hasty Pudding Club. He stays up until a quarter to six and plays billiards at the club until breakfast.

events.detail: Large family dinner at the Lees
All-night gathering at the Hasty Pudding, then billiards until breakfast

tr_quotes.text: The drive home, in the bright, cold moonlight over the smooth, frozen roads was just perfect.

headline: Forty-four hours without sleep
summary: Roosevelt and Jack Tebbets see the family off in Boston. He makes calls with Alice, dines with 'Uncle' Bill Lee and returns for the annual Porcellian dinner, finally going to bed at midnight after 44 hours awake.

events.detail: Sees the family off on their return trip
Calls with Alice and dines with Bill Lee
Annual Porcellian dinner

tr_quotes.text: Got to bed at 12 oclock - after being 44 hours without sleep.

headline: A drive toward Milton
summary: After teaching at the mission school, Roosevelt takes Alice on a long drive to Forest Hills and out toward Milton on a beautiful day.

events.detail: Teaches at the mission school
Long drive with Alice to Forest Hills and toward Milton

uncertain: Diary spells 'Forrest Hill'.

headline: A stormy day with Alice
summary: With rain and snow all day, Roosevelt happily spends nearly every hour with Alice, and his diary overflows with affection for her.

events.detail: Spends the stormy day with Alice

tr_quotes.text: Oh, how I love my little darling!

uncertain: Header says Cambridge, though he appears to have been at the Lees.

headline: Surprise party for Danny Peabody
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge early and that evening joins a surprise gathering at the Rogers home in honor of Danny Peabody.

events.detail: Returns to Cambridge
Surprise party at the Rogers' for Danny Peabody

headline: A day without Chestnut Hill
summary: For once Roosevelt stays away from Chestnut Hill, driving his dogcart in the afternoon and spending the evening at the club. He writes to his uncle John Roosevelt in praise of Alice.

events.detail: Afternoon drive and an evening at the club
Writes Uncle John Roosevelt praising Alice

letters.topic: Speaks warmly of Alice, his new fiancée

tr_quotes.text: For a wonder did not go over to Chestnut Hill

uncertain: The record does not say how John Roosevelt was related to TR; he was likely an uncle.

headline: Dinner at the Bartletts
summary: Roosevelt lunches at Chestnut Hill and takes Alice for a cart ride. In the evening he escorts Alice and Rose to dine with the Bartletts, sitting between Miss Whitney and Miss Sears and spending the rest of the night with Miss Perkins.

events.detail: Lunch at Chestnut Hill and a cart drive with Alice
Dinner at the Bartletts with Alice and Rose

uncertain: 'Miss Whitney' assumed to be Bessie Whitney; 'Rose' may be Rose Lee.

headline: Overnight in Salem with Alice
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge early, then travels to Salem with Alice to stay with the Lees there. He is charmed by the old town and by her company.

events.detail: Goes to Salem with Alice for an overnight visit

tr_quotes.text: Salem is a quaint old place

headline: Lunch for two at Parker's
summary: Roosevelt and Alice return to Boston and share a cozy lunch for two at Parker's. That evening Colonel Russell is his host for dinner at the Somerset Club. It is also Elliott's 20th birthday.

events.detail: Returns from Salem to Boston
Private lunch with Alice at Parker's
Colonel Russell's dinner at the Somerset Club

tr_quotes.text: had a cosy tete-a-tete lunch at Parkers.

uncertain: Diary spells 'Col. Russel'.

headline: Leap Day drive through Milton
summary: After Sunday school Roosevelt drives to Chestnut Hill as usual and takes Alice on a long cart ride through Forest Hills and Milton, staying the night at the Lees. In New York, the Second Avenue elevated railway opens the same day.

events.detail: Teaches Sunday school
Long cart drive with Alice; spends the night at the Lees
New York's Second Avenue elevated line begins service
